trace.claim: The paper asks how partisan polarization varies subnationally and event-driven during COVID-19 pandemic in US and Canada, and how it relates to ideology, conspiracy content and vaccination.
Politically conservative regions showed significantly higher partisan polarization in both countries, especially in the US, and US vaccine polarization negatively correlates with vaccination rates.
The study uses millions of geolocated Twitter tweets from late 2020 classified by party affiliation and topic via RoBERTa embeddings and C-index polarization metric.
Conservative US states and provinces show higher overall polarization on COVID topics.
US vaccine polarization is strongly negatively correlated with actual vaccination rates.
Polarization spikes last only a few days and coincide with specific political events.
Conservative partisans tweet conspiracy content at higher rates, with a small negative correlation to polarization in US.
The authors note the polarization index reflects politically engaged Twitter users and cannot establish causality, and language limitation biases Canadian results.
The authors position their work within computational text embedding studies of polarization and adopt a strictly text-based method due to restricted network data.
